Inclosure 3 in No. 445. 
Mr, Pisani to Lord Stratford de Redelijfe. 


My Lord, Pera, February 20, 1856. 
HAVING read and explained to Fuad Pasha and Mehemed Pasha your 
Excelleney’s instruction to me of yesterday's date, respecting the firman 
containing the Articles of the fourth pomt, the Conyention about brigandage, 
the transfer of the 'Tidjaret, and the Improvement of the eustom-house, &e., 
have now the honour to report that both his Excellency and his Highness told 
me, that you may rest assured that the Sultan’s charter, containing the points 
agreed upon in the Conferences, bears the most authentic and solemn character, 
invested as itis with His Imperial Majesty's hatti-sherif, It is true, added Fuad 
Pasha, that he said to your Excellency that the hatt was to be more 


a47 


comprehensive; but when he said so, there was no question of a preamble 
which subsequently was thought indispensable to give the firman more weight, 
and calculated to show a deeper interest than usual. He repeated again that he 
perfectly enters into your sentiments, and because he and his colleagues felt all 
the importance of investing the Sultan’s charter with all that might impress 
respect upon the people and confidence on foreign nations as to the sincerity 
af the Porte’s Ministers, they gave such publicity and solemnity to its 
promulgation. 

With reference to the execution of the measures proclaimed, both the 
Kaimakam Pasha and Fuad Pasha requested me to tell your Excellency that all 
the measures which can be carried into effect at once will suffer no delay. There 
are others which require time; for instance, ihe formation of tribunals of 
commerce, police, &c. The new Penal Code has already been translated and will 
soon be printed; that of commerce is before a Mixed Commission, a8 your 
Excellency is aware, and immediately the report of that Commission is presented 
to the Porte, the necessary measures will be adopted, 

As regards the pending questions alluded to above, his Excelleney said that. 
the Greck Convention on Brigandage will be communicated to his colleagues im 
the first meeting of the Ministerial Council, most likely on Saturday, or at the 
latest on Sunday. He gave orders, in my presence, to the Amedgi Effendi to 
collect all the papers connected with that matter and have them ready for 
perusal, in the Counell, by Saturday. For the transfer of the Tidjaret he is in 
communication, since yesterday, with the Minister of Commerce. As to the 
improvement of the custom-house, he spoke already to the Minister of Finance, 
under whose control that establishment is placed, und expects his answer. 

[have sounded his Excellency as to the expedience of establishing a Crédit- 
Mobilier Bank. 1 found him very well disposed, and he requests your 
Excellency to tell the person whom you recommend to present his plan in 
writing to the Porte; and should what he proposes be acceptable to them, they 
will talk over the matter with him i order to come to an understanding. 

I have, &e. { 
(Signed) ET. PISANI.

Lord Stratford de Redcliffe to the Earl of Clarendon.—( Received at Paris

(Telegraphic. Constantinople, March 5, 1856. 

INTELLIGENCE reaches us from Russia, confirms, more or less, the 
impression (lerived from other sourees that the war is felt severely in that 
country, that distress and embarrassment prevail there, and that the desire for 
peace 1s universal. 

Such, in particular, is the substance of information given secretly to the 
British Consul at ‘Tehran by the first interpreter of the Persian Embassy at 
St, Petersburgh, recently arrived there from Russia.

The Rarl of Clarendon to Lord Stratford de Redcliffe. 
(No. 259.) 
My Lord, Foreign Office, March 5, 1896. 

HER Majesty's Government have had under consideration your Excelleney’s 
despatch No, 170 of the 12th ultimo, in which you inclose copy of the official note 
addressed to you by Fuad Pasha relating to the ease of renegades in Turkey. 

1 have to state to your Excellency that Her Majesty's Government are 
satisfied with the reply which the Porte has thus made to the representations of 
Her Majesty's Government on this subject, and they consider that the declara- 
tions contained in Fuad Pasha’s note may be effectually appealed to hereafter, 


if any renewal should take place of molestation of converts from Islam to 
Christianity. 


Tam, &e. | 
(Signed) CLARENDON.

It is supposed that the French have Russian prisoners of suitable rank who
